title: counting-block-fires-its-clock-probes-on-its-own-pulse
intention: The counting_block component fires its own clock probes (raise_rate_falls) from its groundloop/pulse.py on each heartbeat, so they run again now that the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/.
why: Since bae622881f03 PROVED (2026-09-30) the heartbeat no longer discovers probes/ folders; it calls only groundloop/pulse.py files. So raise_rate_falls is dark: the only firing left is one pass at web-server start through bus_client's private GroundLoopDevice, which ticket efb670ff1dd8 removes. That is the lived symptom: raise_rate_falls reads the table the block wrote on the last beat and compares the raise rate per 200 post-arming appends against the first 200 (ticket 5a4ec289bf15), and nobody is looking. counting_block ALREADY has cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py (block.pulse()); the probe is added to that module after the fold, not a second pulse file.
traces_to: Law 6 and Law 1 via ticket bae622881f03 (PROVED 2026-09-30): the heartbeat calls each groundloop/pulse.py and nothing else, and Akien ruled clock probes are 'tickled by the system device or their owning devices (from the ground loop pulse)'. The owner fires its own watch.
how: Compose the shared tool cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py built by ticket 32959e65ec5a (do not copy its logic). add to cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py: a module-level BeatProbes('counting_block', <this folder>, ['raise_rate_falls'], bus) and on_pulse(now, context) returning its pulse record. Only the named probes fire; counting_block ALREADY has cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py (block.pulse()); the probe is added to that module after the fold, not a second pulse file. The probe files stay where they are, unchanged.
falsifier: Proof cairn/machines/counting_block/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py: (1) discovery.pulse_sites() lists cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py at class level; (2) the module's BeatProbes names exactly ['raise_rate_falls'] and each resolves to a Probe; (3) other modules in cairn/machines/counting_block/probes/ are not in its roster; (4) on_pulse(now, {}) with a recording stub bus returns a record whose fired+held entries cover exactly those probes. Live horizon: three consecutive beats of ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json list the counting_block trigger ok. Wrong intent if one of these probes turns out to be event-driven rather than clock-driven.
watchme: none, because the probes being moved ARE the watches (cairn/machines/counting_block/probes/raise_rate_falls.py), each keeping its own ticket's WATCHME, and whether they fire is read on every beat in the heartbeat's own record ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json (the counting_block trigger's ok flag and pulse record).
assumption_check: (1) raise_rate_falls is clock probes (Akien's group-2 list, 2026-09-30). (2) The heartbeat calls on_pulse(now, {}) once per 60s beat and holds the module between beats, re-loading it when cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py changes, which resets crossing memory; a reset re-pokes a still-true condition once, which is acceptable and matches a loop restart under the old runner. (3) A probe's poke needs a bus; connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False) gives one without beating. (4) The probe files are unchanged; only who fires them moves.
missing_check: (a) This depends on 32959e65ec5a (the shared cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py); it waits at BUILDME until that is PROVED. (b) counting_block ALREADY has cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py (block.pulse()); the probe is added to that module after the fold, not a second pulse file.
builder_check: WHERE: edit cairn/machines/counting_block/groundloop/pulse.py and new cairn/machines/counting_block/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py. HOW: from cairn.tools.base.beat_probes import BeatProbes; module level _PROBES = BeatProbes('counting_block', Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], ['raise_rate_falls'], bus=<lazy connect_bus(devices=[], beat=False)>); on_pulse(now, context) returns _PROBES.on_pulse(now, context) merged into the existing return dict under key probes. The helper's exact constructor is whatever 32959e65ec5a built: read cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py first. TESTS use a stub bus and never fire the real triggers (the census/DB reads are slow); assert the roster, not the firing, which the helper's own proof covers. DO NOT move or edit the probe files.
